question.text: If $\quad y(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin x & \cos x & \sin x+\cos x+1 \\ 27 & 28 & 27 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right|, x \in \mathbb{R}$, then $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}+y$ is equal to

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & C_3 \rightarrow C_3-C_1 \\ & y(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin x & \cos x & 1+\cos x \\ 27 & 28 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right| \\ & y(x)=-(1+\cos x) \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=\sin x \\ & \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\cos x \\ & \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}+y=-1\end{aligned}$
